sentences.text: Fritz Erich Georg Eduard von Lewinski , known as Erich von Manstein -LRB- 24 November 1887 -- 9 June 1973 -RRB- , was a German commander of the Wehrmacht , Nazi Germany 's armed forces during the Second World War .	Eduard von Lewinski	Eduard von Lewinski	Wehrmacht	Wehrmacht	Nazi Germany	Nazi Germany	Second World War	Second World War
He attained the rank of field marshal .	field marshal	Field Marshal (Germany)

Born into an aristocratic Prussian family with a long history of military service , Manstein joined the army at a young age and saw service on Western Front and Eastern Front during the First World War -LRB- 1914 -- 18 -RRB- .	Western Front	Western Front (World War I)	Eastern Front	Eastern Front (World War I)	First World War	First World War
He rose to the rank of captain by the end of the war and was active in the inter-war period helping Germany rebuild her armed forces .

In September 1939 , during the invasion of Poland at the beginning of the Second World War , he was serving as Chief of Staff to Gerd von Rundstedt 's Army Group South .	Army Group South	Army Group South	Second World War	Second World War	invasion of Poland	invasion of Poland	Gerd von Rundstedt	Gerd von Rundstedt

Adolf Hitler chose Manstein 's strategy for the invasion of France of May 1940 , a plan later refined by Franz Halder and other members of the OKH .	Adolf Hitler	Adolf Hitler	invasion of France	Battle of France	Franz Halder	Franz Halder	OKH	OKH

Anticipating a firm Allied reaction should the main thrust of the invasion take place through the Netherlands , Manstein devised an innovative operation -- later known as the Sichelschnitt -LRB- `` sickle cut '' -RRB- -- that called for an attack through the woods of the Ardennes and a rapid drive to the English Channel , thus cutting off the French and Allied armies in Belgium and Flanders .	operation	Operational level of war	Ardennes	Ardennes	English Channel	English Channel	Belgium	Belgium	Flanders	Flanders

Attaining the rank of general at the end of the campaign , he was active in the invasion of the Soviet Union in June 1941 and the Siege of Sevastopol -LRB- 1941 -- 1942 -RRB- , and was promoted to field marshal on 1 July 1942 .	Siege of Sevastopol	Siege of Sevastopol (1941–42)	field marshal	Field Marshal (Germany)	general	general (Germany)	invasion of the Soviet Union	Operation Barbarossa
He also participated in the Siege of Leningrad .	Siege of Leningrad	Siege of Leningrad

Germany 's fortunes in the war began to take an unfavourable turn later in 1942 , especially in the catastrophic Battle of Stalingrad , where Manstein commanded a failed relief effort -LRB- `` Operation Winter Storm '' -RRB- in December .	Battle of Stalingrad	Battle of Stalingrad	Operation Winter Storm	Operation Winter Storm

Later known as the `` backhand blow '' , Manstein 's counteroffensive in the Third Battle of Kharkov -LRB- February -- March 1943 -RRB- regained substantial territory and resulted in the destruction of three Soviet armies and the retreat of three others .	Third Battle of Kharkov	Third Battle of Kharkov
He was one of the primary commanders at the Battle of Kursk -LRB- July -- August 1943 -RRB- , one of the largest tank battles in history .	Battle of Kursk	Battle of Kursk
His ongoing disagreements with Hitler over the conduct of the war led to his dismissal in March 1944 .
He never obtained another command and was taken prisoner by the British in August 1945 , several months after Germany 's defeat .

Manstein gave testimony at the main Nuremberg trials of war criminals in August 1946 , and prepared a paper that , along with his later memoirs , helped cultivate the myth of a `` clean Wehrmacht '' -- the myth that the German armed forces were not culpable for the atrocities of the Holocaust .	Wehrmacht	Wehrmacht	Nuremberg trials	Nuremberg trials	clean Wehrmacht	clean Wehrmacht	the Holocaust	the Holocaust

In 1949 he was tried in Hamburg for war crimes and was convicted on nine of seventeen counts , including the poor treatment of prisoners of war and failing to protect civilian lives in his sphere of operations .	was tried	Trial of Erich von Manstein	Hamburg	Hamburg
His sentence of eighteen years in prison was later reduced to twelve , and he served only four years before being released in 1953 .
As a military advisor to the West German government in the mid-1950s , he helped re-establish the armed forces .	West German	West Germany

His memoir , Verlorene Siege -LRB- 1955 -RRB- , translated into English as Lost Victories , was highly critical of Hitler 's leadership , and only dealt with the military aspects of the war , ignoring its political and ethical contexts .	Verlorene Siege	Verlorene Siege
Manstein died in Munich in 1973 .	Munich	Munich
